reference.one_line: 33-year-old man, hospital day 6 of Staphylococcus aureus endocarditis of two valves with septic lung emboli; improving on cefazolin, but vancomycin is still running and creatinine is 1.4.

handoff.summary: Teodor Penhallurick, 33, has methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus endocarditis with a 1.6 cm tricuspid and a 0.7 cm mitral vegetation, a small patent foramen ovale and cavitating septic lung emboli. He is improving on cefazolin (temperature 37.2, white cells 10.4, room air). Vancomycin was never stopped: the trough was 22.4 on 16 Nov, creatinine has risen from 0.9 to 1.4 and a dose is due at 21:00. No culture was drawn on 15 Nov, so the first negative set is 16 Nov (still preliminary) and the long line is not yet due, whatever today's note says. Pleuritic pain flared to 8 of 10 overnight and he nearly left; he is on buprenorphine-naloxone 8 mg/2 mg three times daily and agreed to stay.
to_do: Discontinue vancomycin before the 21:00 dose and call the pharmacist back
Do not place the long line until infectious diseases approve (48 to 72 hours of negative cultures from 16 Nov)
Correct the course dates: six weeks from 16 Nov ends 28 Dec
Creatinine tomorrow; oral fluids 2 L; no anti-inflammatory drugs or contrast
Ask addiction medicine to review pain today, as he was promised
if_then: If new weakness, speech change, visual loss or a cold painful limb, then urgent brain or limb imaging and call cardiac surgery (embolus through the foramen ovale)
If PR interval lengthens beyond 200 ms, heart failure appears or fever returns above 38.5 °C, then repeat echo and call cardiology and surgery
If he says he is leaving, then call the resident and addiction medicine, treat pain and withdrawal first, and make sure he has naloxone, buprenorphine and a follow-up plan however he leaves

reference.brief_hospital_course: Mr Penhallurick, 33, who injects fentanyl and has had no fixed address since August, was admitted on 12 Nov with sepsis (39.6 °C, heart rate 128, blood pressure 96/52), blood-streaked sputum and a left forearm abscess, which was drained. He had been unwell since about 1 Nov and had attended an emergency department on 5 Nov. Blood cultures on 12, 13 and 14 Nov grew methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus. CT showed cavitating septic pulmonary emboli; transoesophageal echo on 16 Nov showed a 1.6 cm tricuspid vegetation with severe regurgitation, a 0.7 cm mitral vegetation, a small patent foramen ovale and no abscess. Vancomycin was started on 12 Nov and cefazolin on 14 Nov. Vancomycin was continued in error; the trough reached 22.4 mcg/mL and creatinine rose from 0.9 to 1.4 mg/dL. No culture was collected on 15 Nov; the first negative sets were drawn on 16 Nov, so six weeks of treatment runs to 28 Dec. Cardiac surgery found no urgent indication. Opioid withdrawal was treated with buprenorphine-naloxone from 13 Nov, now 8 mg/2 mg three times daily; pleuritic pain remains troublesome. Hepatitis C is active and he is not immune to hepatitis B. No safe discharge setting has yet been found.

qa.q: What did the transoesophageal echo show?
qa.a: Tricuspid vegetation 1.6 × 0.9 cm with severe regurgitation; mitral vegetation 0.7 cm with mild to moderate regurgitation; no abscess; small patent foramen ovale; ejection fraction 60%.

qa.q: What are his hepatitis and HIV results?
qa.a: HIV not detected. Hepatitis C RNA 1,240,000 IU/mL (active infection). Not immune to hepatitis B.

qa.q: What is the current buprenorphine-naloxone dose and when is it next due?
qa.a: 8 mg/2 mg under the tongue three times daily; last given 17 Nov 14:05, next due 20:00.
0.9 on 12 and 14 Nov, 1.1 on 15 Nov, 1.3 on 16 Nov, 1.4 on 17 Nov.
Yes. White cells 19.8 to 10.4, C-reactive protein 248 to 96, procalcitonin 8.4 to 1.2, platelets recovered from 104 to 236, temperature 38.9 on 15 Nov to 37.2, and off oxygen since midnight.

qa.q: On what date was the first negative blood culture drawn, and when does six weeks end?
qa.a: 16 Nov at 06:05 (still preliminary). Nothing was drawn on 15 Nov. Six weeks from 16 Nov ends 28 Dec, not 27 Dec.
evidence: micro: 16 Nov set with laboratory comment

qa.q: How long was he unwell before the first antibiotic?
qa.a: About 11 days: chills began around 1 Nov, after injecting with a reused needle on 31 Oct; vancomycin was first given 12 Nov at 21:30.

qa.q: Why is buprenorphine given three times a day instead of once?
qa.a: Its pain-relieving effect lasts 6 to 8 hours, so divided doses treat his pleuritic pain as well as withdrawal.

qa.q: Why does the patent foramen ovale matter?
qa.a: It gives fragments of the tricuspid vegetation a route to the left side, so a brain or limb embolus is possible and would prompt surgical review.

qa.q: Why is he on only preventive enoxaparin with emboli in the lungs?
qa.a: They are septic emboli, not clot; CT showed no filling defect and infectious diseases advised against full-dose anticoagulation.

qa.q: Did addiction medicine review his pain on 17 Nov as promised overnight?
qa.a: The chart does not say; no addiction medicine note or dose change is recorded by 14:30.

qa.q: Did anyone answer the pharmacist's pages about vancomycin?
qa.a: Not documented. Pages at 11:35 and 13:10 on 16 Nov had no call back, and the order is still active.

epilogue.note: What happens AFTER 'now' in this simulated world. Never shown in the chart; for outcome-prediction ground truth.
epilogue.course: The line request went to infectious diseases for approval, and Dr. Okwuosa-Thorne, checking the cultures, found no 15 Nov set and vancomycin still charted. Vancomycin was stopped before the 21:00 dose and the end date corrected to 28 Dec. Creatinine peaked at 1.6 on 18 Nov and was 1.0 by 24 Nov. Addiction medicine saw him that evening and re-divided the same 24 mg of buprenorphine into four doses a day; he did not try to leave again. The line went in on 19 Nov. Repeat echo on 25 Nov showed smaller vegetations and no abscess, and cultures stayed negative. With no facility willing, he had a long-acting antibiotic (dalbavancin 1,500 mg) on 1 and 8 Dec and moved to a medical respite bed on 2 Dec with a buprenorphine prescriber and hepatitis C appointment. He completed treatment on 28 Dec.

events.event: Infectious diseases review: no 15 Nov culture, long line deferred, end date 28 Dec; vancomycin discontinued
Addiction medicine review: buprenorphine-naloxone re-divided to 6 mg/1.5 mg four times daily (same daily total)
Long line placed after 72 hours of negative cultures; first hepatitis B vaccine dose
Repeat echo: tricuspid vegetation 1.4 cm, mitral 0.6 cm, no abscess
Dalbavancin 1,500 mg, first dose; long line removed
Dalbavancin second dose at infusion clinic
Emergency visit for temperature 37.9 °C: blood cultures taken and negative, viral illness, sent back to respite

outcomes_30_day.notable: Completed antibiotics 28 Dec; still on buprenorphine at 30 days, with one lapse he reported himself to his prescriber.

portal_messages.subject: still sick after ER yesterday
portal_messages.body: i was in the ER yesterday they said its a virus. i left before the papers because i was getting sick from waiting. but i been having shaking chills and soaking sweats most of a week now and its not getting better. i never got the antibiotics filled in september. can somebody just send some to the pharmacy. i dont have a ride to keep coming back

No judgement about leaving; give a direct number

conversation.setting: Bedside on 4 East (4E-14), 13 Nov about 14:20, addiction medicine consult

turns.speaker: Dr. Lindgren-Achieng
turns.text: Mr Penhallurick? I'm Dr. Lindgren-Achieng, addiction medicine. The team asked me to help with the withdrawal and the pain. Can I sit?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah. Teo's fine. I feel like death, so.

turns.speaker: Dr. Lindgren-Achieng
turns.text: I can see the gooseflesh from here. When did you last use?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yesterday, like three in the afternoon. Before I came in.

turns.speaker: Dr. Lindgren-Achieng
turns.text: So about a day. And it's fentanyl now?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah. About a gram a day. Six, eight times, in my arms mostly.

turns.speaker: Dr. Lindgren-Achieng
turns.text: How did it start, if you don't mind?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Fell off a roof. Work. Twenty twenty-one. They put a plate in my leg and gave me oxys, and then... they stopped giving them. Heroin after that, snorting, then the needle in twenty-three.

turns.speaker: Dr. Lindgren-Achieng
turns.text: That's a very common road. Needles: new each time, or reusing?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Reuse. I rinse them. Tap water.

turns.speaker: Dr. Lindgren-Achieng
turns.text: Okay. I ask because of the heart infection, not to tell you off. When did you first feel ill with this?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Honestly? I been sick since Halloween weekend. I used an old one on the thirty-first and next day I had the shakes, sweating through my shirt. The arm blew up later.

turns.speaker: Dr. Lindgren-Achieng
turns.text: So nearly two weeks, not three days.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I went to an ER on the fifth. They said virus.

turns.speaker: Dr. Lindgren-Achieng
turns.text: I'm sorry that was missed. Have you overdosed?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Once. June. Woke up in my van with the medics over me.

turns.speaker: Dr. Lindgren-Achieng
turns.text: Ever been on treatment? Methadone, buprenorphine?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No. They offered in June, I said no. I'd take it now. Last time I was in a hospital I walked out day two 'cause nobody did anything for this.

turns.speaker: Dr. Lindgren-Achieng
turns.text: That won't be the plan here. You're in clear withdrawal, which is actually what we need to start buprenorphine safely. First dose at half past three, four milligrams under the tongue, and again every two hours up to twelve today. Sixteen tomorrow.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: And the pain? When I breathe in it's like a knife.

turns.speaker: Dr. Lindgren-Achieng
turns.text: That pain is real; you've got infection in the lungs. From the fifteenth we'll split the buprenorphine three times a day, because it works on pain for six to eight hours. Plus regular acetaminophen and a numbing patch.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: So no more of the IV stuff from last night.

turns.speaker: Dr. Lindgren-Achieng
turns.text: No, the hydromorphone stops now. Once buprenorphine is on board it would hardly work anyway. There's clonidine for the restless legs and something for the nerves if you ask.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: They're gonna think I'm drug seeking if I ask.

turns.speaker: Dr. Lindgren-Achieng
turns.text: I'm writing in my note that nobody is to use that word. Tell me the plan back, so I know I was clear.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Strip under my tongue at three thirty, more every couple hours. Three times a day later for the pain. No IV.

turns.speaker: Dr. Lindgren-Achieng
turns.text: That's it. And before you leave here, however you leave, you'll have a naloxone kit, clean supplies and an appointment with someone who prescribes this.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay. Thanks for not... yeah. Thanks.
